decisions.statement: The edits are kept in a file beside the page of the answering agent.
The edits outlive the page the file sits beside.
A path that is no page keeps no edits.
One line has one edit written as JSON.
A line states one edit of the six kinds and no body that edit does not name.
A line is read as the edit that line states rather than against any body.
A line reading as no edit refuses the whole file rather than being passed over.
That refusal names the line the reading stopped at.
A refusal counts its line from the first row of the first numbered file.
The rows are answered in the order the rows were appended.
A change appends its rows rather than writing the file again.
A row appended states the edit as the answering change stated the edit.
A row comes back as the row went in.
A row is appended to the last numbered file rather than to a file written anew.
A row rolls into the next numbered file where the ceiling is reached.
A row larger than the ceiling is alone in the file that row opens.
A file's fill is read from its size rather than from its text.
An append answers the rows appended rather than every row kept.
An append reads no row already kept.
A settle whose rows open with the rows read appends only the rows past the rows read.
A settle whose rows open otherwise takes the files away and writes the files again.
A writer takes a turn over the file before appending.
The lines a caller already has are dropped as lines rather than as edits.
A drop finding other lines at the front leaves every line where those lines are.
A reader taking no turn can meet a row a write left half appended.
The folder with the page is made before the turn over the file is taken.
A file left holding no row is taken away rather than left empty.
The edits a subagent leaves stay in the file the subagent kept the edits in.
One subagent's edits are read and taken away apart from another's.
A page with a file of edits beside that page has edits waiting.
Whether edits wait is answered from the first file rather than from the rows.
The rows are folded into one answer by the rule one answer is gathered by.
A body beneath is read as bytes and decoded rather than read as characters.
A body the decoding will not read is answered as not text rather than as no body.
Nothing here works out a body or judges an edit.
A row names no commit the edit in that row was composed against.
A sweep keeps nothing of the rows swept.
A sweep of every row takes the files away without reading a row.
A line reading as no edit refuses a reader of the rows and refuses no sweep.
A sweep answers whether a file was there to take away.
A row swept is read back with its agent, its paths, and the commit it was composed against.

definition: the edits an agent has answered and not landed, appended beside the agent's page
